Issue #5: Better handling of links to other sites

We render our product docs with Python-Markdown and readers keep complaining that when they click a link to another website they lose their place in the docs. Other tools we've tried seem to handle external links better out of the box.

Could Python-Markdown do something smarter with external links? I'm not sure what the best approach is, just that the current behaviour isn't great for documentation sites.


--- maintainer comment 1 by @AvAdiii ---
Thanks for the questions. Decisions:

1. Add a new built-in extension called `external_links`, loaded with `extensions=['external_links']`. Nothing changes unless it is enabled.
2. A link is external when its `href` starts with `http://` or `https://`. Relative links, `#anchors` and `mailto:` links are not external.
3. Every external `<a>` element gets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. This includes automatic links like `<https://example.com>`.
4. Images are not affected. No configuration options for now.
</untrusted-issue nonce="80a51a886ec0">
